about: What tools/gallery.mjs writes into examples/index.html besides what it reads from docs/types.md, tools/types.json and the models: the map type's own name and description, each type card's picture alt text (the picture is the first view of its type page, examples/types/<type>.html), and the Atlas's entry. tests/gallery.test.mjs fails when the committed page is not what the tool writes.

retired.about: Models of examples/ the gallery does not show: bike-share.json, the hidden test and bench model, and bike-share-c4.json, what umlimator.py import writes from its Structurizr source, examples/bike-share.dsl. The real-world models that left the gallery on 19 Nov 2026 (the maintainer's decision) were deleted when the bike share model took over their tests. No card, link or mention of these is on the gallery, the docs or the README; the site still renders them.

map.name: Map
map.text: Layered architecture maps: cards, lines and boxes in views that open into each other, with stories, tours and lenses.

alts.map: Card shapes: people, a browser app, a phone, a window, a terminal, an agent, a database, a queue, a file, a package, hosts and a hook around a shop's API
alts.uml-class: A UML class diagram of a bookshop's sales domain: Customer, Order, OrderLine, Book, an abstract Payment and its CardPayment, the Payable interface, the OrderStatus enumeration, the Money data type and a note
alts.uml-object: A UML object diagram of one placed order: ada, a Customer, linked to order1042, an Order, its two order lines, the books they are for and the card payment, each with its slots
alts.uml-package: A UML package diagram of a bookshop: the packages shared, catalog, sales, payments with card inside it, and wholesale, each a box holding its classes, joined by imports, an access, a merge and a dependency, and the profile BookshopConventions, a closed folder that sales applies
alts.uml-composite-structure: A UML composite structure diagram of an order service: its ports on its border, four parts, two of them showing their types' ports, connectors between them, an open collaboration as a dashed ellipse and a collaboration use with its role bindings
alts.uml-component: A UML component diagram of a bookshop: Shop API a box holding Checkout, ports on their borders with delegations between them, Orders as a ball with a socket, SignIn as a rectangle, an artifact manifesting Shop API
alts.uml-deployment: A UML deployment diagram of a bookshop in production: devices and execution environments drawn as cubes and nested, artifacts deployed in them, communication paths labelled with their protocols
alts.uml-profile: A UML profile diagram of a bookshop's modelling conventions: a profile holding metaclasses and stereotypes with their tag definitions, extensions with filled triangles, one marked required, a package applying the profile, and a class showing its stereotypes' tags
alts.uml-use-case: A UML use case diagram of a bookshop: a shopper, a member and a payment provider as stick figures, eight use cases as ellipses in the Online bookshop subject, includes and extends drawn dashed with their labels
alts.uml-activity: A UML activity diagram of fulfilling an order in three lanes, Order worker, Warehouse and Email service: actions, an object node, a data store, a decision and a merge, a fork and a join, and a flow final
alts.uml-state-machine: A UML state machine diagram of an order's life: Placed with its activities, a choice, a fork into the Parcel and Payment regions of Fulfilling, In delivery with a history, Cancelled and a terminate
alts.uml-sequence: A UML sequence diagram of a bookshop's checkout: a shopper, the storefront, the api, payments and a receipt created on the way, their messages in time order with activation bars, an alt frame with an opt frame and an interaction use inside it
alts.uml-communication: A UML communication diagram of the same checkout: five lifelines joined by connectors, each link's messages a stack of numbered rows
alts.uml-interaction-overview: A UML interaction overview diagram of buying a book: interaction uses for finding a book, checking out and emailing the receipt, a decision looping back through a merge, a fork and a join, and an inline interaction with its three lifelines
alts.uml-timing: A UML timing diagram of one charge: two lifelines as step lines through their states on a time ruler in milliseconds, a call and its reply between them at their times, a duration constraint and a time constraint
alts.uml-information-flow: A UML information flow diagram of what travels with an order: a shopper, components and information items, joined by dashed flow lines each naming what it conveys
alts.sysml-requirement: A SysML requirement diagram of a city e-bike in a req frame: requirements with their ids and wrapped texts, containment crosshairs, blocks satisfying and test cases verifying them
alts.sysml-block-definition: A SysML block definition diagram of a city e-bike in a bdd frame: blocks with named compartments of parts, values, constraints and ports, an interface block, constraint blocks and value types
alts.sysml-internal-block: A SysML internal block diagram of a city e-bike: the bike as the ibd frame holding its parts, ports on their borders with flow arrows, connectors carrying DC power and phase current
alts.sysml-parametric: A SysML parametric diagram of a city e-bike's range: constraint properties with rounded corners and their expressions, parameters on their borders bound to value properties
alts.c4: A C4 system context diagram of a bookshop: the shopper and staff as people, the bookshop as the system in the middle, the external systems it uses in grey
alts.er: An entity-relationship diagram of a bookshop's database: seven tables with their key columns first, related by crow's foot ends, identifying lines solid and the rest dashed
alts.dfd: A data flow diagram of a bookshop, level 1: three external entities, three numbered processes and two data stores, joined by labelled data flows
alts.flowchart: A flowchart of handling a returned book, laid out down: a start, input and manual input, a decision with yes and no exits, a delay, a database, a document, a connector and an end
alts.bpmn: A BPMN diagram of a bookshop's order to shipment: three pools, the bookshop's in two lanes, tasks, events and gateways joined by sequence flows, dashed message flows between the pools, a timer on the payment task's border
alts.mindmap: A mindmap of opening a bookshop: the root in the middle, six branches left and right, each in its own colour, joined by curves
alts.aws: An AWS architecture diagram of a bookshop: a cloud, a region, a VPC, two availability zones, public and private subnets and a security group as nested boxes, fifteen services and resources drawn with their icons and full service names
alts.gcp: A Google Cloud architecture diagram of a bookshop: a project, a region, a network, a subnetwork and two zones as nested boxes, nine products drawn with their icons and full service names
alts.azure: An Azure architecture diagram of a bookshop: a subscription, a resource group, a region, a virtual network and two subnets as nested boxes, eight services drawn with their icons and full service names

atlas.name: The Umlimator Atlas
atlas.text: Umlimator's own model, drawn with umlimator: its parts and who uses each (a map), its system context and containers (C4), the core module's packages in build order (a package diagram), the typed diagram families (a component diagram), the diff Action on a pull request (a sequence diagram) and umlimator's state machines (navigation, the story player, tours, the page's keys and the MCP page), joined by cards that open them.
atlas.alt: The Umlimator Atlas's overview: the author, an AI assistant, the map-repo skill, the model JSON, umlimator.py, the readers, the module, umlimator/all, the page, the MCP page, the host page, the element, the docs site and the diff Action, with GitHub and Chrome
stories: A pull request, from push to comment

views.overview: The atlas's root: umlimator's parts and who uses each, the Python parts in a box, line kinds (feeds, state, triggers) and weights, two cards whose views a host may load when opened, and a story along a pull request.
views.context: The system context: the author and the reader as people, umlimator as the system, the AI assistant, GitHub and Chrome as external systems.
views.containers: The containers inside umlimator's dashed boundary, each with its technology, and the relationships the context implies.
views.layers: The core module's packages in src/, in the order tools/build.mjs concatenates them into lib/umlimator.js.
views.registry: The typed families as components, each depending on the core's registry, which the typed canvas looks up.
views.diff-run: The diff Action on a pull request: an async start, calls and their replies, a self-call, and an alt frame on whether the token can write.
views.machines: How umlimator's machines relate: the page and the MCP page drive render()'s handle, a box holding the story player, navigation and tours, which report every change to MapState.
views.navigation: Navigation's states, a move at a time, with its loops back and run order numbered.
views.story: The story player's states, from entering a step to ended or stopped.
views.tour: A tour's or a replay's states: riding, held, at the end or cut short.
views.keys: The order the page's keys close its layers in, as boxes of states.
views.mcp: A page tool, step by step, from the assistant's call to the answer once a page has shown it.
